- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add 1–2% downward correction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1% lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 75% of forecast, apply “floor correction” — cap forecast at 75% of prior 30-day average + 5% buffer.
